title: Redistribute warmstart credits to address token starvation in mixed-variant routing
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers reported increased TTFT and reduced tokens/sec for short-turn chat sessions after the mixed-variant consolidation rollout on 2026-03-12. Root cause appears to be a regression in the warmstart credit accounting that allowed aggressive variants (longer KV warmups) to consume session warmstart credits for the shared variant pool, starving subsequent short-turn sessions and causing first-token delays and throughput collapse on multiplexed workers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket implements a short-term hotpatch to redistribute warmstart credits per-session and add a conservative backstop to the variant consolidation router to preserve short-turn throughput while we design a robust quota-based allocation.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use workload generator with mix: 60% short-turn (1-8 tokens reply), 40% long-turn (200-800 tokens), targeting single multiplexed worker pool.
2) Deploy quantized variant-consolidation branch on staging (branch: variant-consolidation-2026-03) and run at 1500 req/s.
3) Observe warmstart_credit_utilization metric rising above 80% and short-turn TTFT median increasing by 2.5x within 12 minutes.
4) Confirm production traces (trace IDs in SOC dashboard) show KV warmups blocking tokenization tasks for new sessions.
5) Failover test: compare behavior with warmstart_credits_per_session=1 vs=3.
root_cause: A bookkeeping regression introduced during variant consolidation changed credit decrement timing. Long-turn variants consume initial warmstart credits synchronously, preventing credits from being assigned to rapidly arriving short-turn sessions. The router lacked a per-session minimum allotment and the prioritization heuristic favored active KV cache reuse without considering expected reply-length distribution.
mitigation: Implemented hotpatch that: (1) enforces warmstart_credits_per_session default=2 for all sessions; (2) adds a fast-path in the router that reserves 1 credit for sessions with predicted short-turn behavior; (3) introduces a soft quota 'fair_share_backstop' that triggers probabilistic throttling of warm prefetch for variants once per-tenant warmstart usage exceeds threshold; (4) telemetry alerting for warmstart_credit_utilization > 70%.
rollout_plan: Canary (10% traffic, hosted-only) - runtime-2.3.1-hotfix canary at 2026-03-14 11:00 UTC; monitor 30m
Ramp to 50% (hosted + dedicated low-impact regions) - 2026-03-14 13:00 UTC; monitor 1h
Full rollout for Hosted + Dedicated - 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC after signoff
Private deployments: provide patch bundle and rollout notes; advise customers to apply during low-traffic window; target completion 2026-03-18
monitoring: SLO checks: TTFT P50, P95 for short-turn sessions monitored per-region
logs: tag traces with 'ws_hotpatch_v2' for post-rollout correlation
